title: 写真に写る前に
paragraphs: Rina was preparing a photo page for her class website. She had many pictures from a recent school trip. Her favorite showed three friends laughing beside a river. She wanted to upload it immediately, but the class website leader asked her to check with everyone in the picture first. Rina thought that this would take unnecessary time because the picture looked cheerful.
リナはクラスのウェブサイト用に写真ページを準備していた。遠足の写真が多く、お気に入りは川辺で笑う友人三人だった。すぐ掲載したかったが、担当者は写る全員に先に確認するよう頼んだ。楽しそうな写真なので無駄な時間だと思った。

Two friends agreed, but the third asked her to choose another image. [1] Rina had never noticed that the friend's name was clearly visible on a bag. The friend was happy to share memories with classmates but did not want that detail on a public page. Rina chose a picture of the river instead.
二人は了承したが、三人目は別の画像を求めた。その友人は、かばんの名前が公のページに出ることを望んでいなかった。リナはそれまで名前がはっきり写っていると気づかなかった。級友と思い出を共有するのはうれしくても、その情報は公開したくなかったのだ。代わりに川の写真を選んだ。

The finished page included places, food, and pictures that everyone had approved. It still looked lively. Rina learned that asking first did not prevent people from sharing an experience. It helped them share it in a way that everyone could feel comfortable with, even after the trip was over.
完成ページには場所、食べ物、全員が了承した写真が載り、十分生き生きしていた。先に尋ねても体験共有を妨げるわけではなく、遠足後も皆が安心できる形で共有できるとリナは学んだ。
questions: 空所[1]に最も合う文は？
He did not want his name to be shown online.
He wanted every photograph printed larger.
He had never been on the school trip.
He asked Rina to remove the river.
次の文のかばんの名前につながる。
大きさの希望ではない。
本人も写真に写っている。
川は代わりに選んだ写真。
the friend's name was clearly visible on a bag
最初に確認を求めたのは誰？
The class website leader.
A stranger near the river.
A bus company worker.
All visitors to the website.
サイト担当者が求めた。
通行人ではない。
バス会社ではない。
閲覧者全員ではない。
the class website leader asked her to check
リナが代わりに選んだ写真は？
The river.
A larger image of the bag.
The friend's private room.
An old class test.
川の写真を選んだ。
かばんを拡大していない。
私室を掲載していない。
試験ではない。
Rina chose a picture of the river instead.
syntax: Rina chose a picture of the river instead.
リナは代わりに川の写真を選んだ。
of the riverはpictureを説明する。insteadが選択の変更を示す。

title: 比べる条件をそろえる
paragraphs: Two students wanted to find out whether covering a bowl would keep water from disappearing quickly. They put one bowl near a sunny window and another in a dark corner. The bowl by the window had a cover, while the other did not. After several days, they compared the water levels. They were excited about presenting the difference to their science class.
生徒二人は、器にふたをすると水が減る速さを抑えられるか調べようとした。一つを日当たりのよい窓辺、もう一つを暗い隅に置いた。窓側にはふたがあり、他方にはなかった。数日後に水位を比べ、違いを発表するのを楽しみにした。

Their teacher looked at the drawings of the experiment. [1] The students had changed both the covers and the locations. They could not be sure which difference had affected the water. So they began again, this time placing the two bowls side by side. They used equal amounts of water and checked them at the same time each day.
先生は実験図を見て、二つの器の場所は同じか尋ねた。生徒はふたと場所の両方を変えており、どちらが水に影響したか確信できなかった。そこでやり直し、器を並べ、同量の水を入れて毎日同時刻に確認した。

The second experiment took another week, but the students understood their question much better. Their presentation included both attempts. They explained why the first comparison had been difficult to understand. For them, learning science now included improving a question and a method, not just obtaining an interesting result.
二回目にもう一週間かかったが、問いをより理解できた。発表には両方の試みを入れ、最初の比較が解釈しにくい理由を説明した。科学を学ぶのは面白い結果を得るだけでなく、問いと方法をよくすることも含むと考えるようになった。
questions: 空所[1]に合う文は？
She asked whether both bowls had been in the same place.
She said that drawings were never useful.
She asked them to stop using water forever.
She announced the result without reading anything.
場所も違ったという次の説明につながる。
図を実際に確認した。
水の永久禁止ではない。
結果を勝手に断定していない。
The students had changed both the covers and the locations.
二回目にそろえた条件は？
Water amounts and checking times.
Only the colors of their clothes.
The names of every classmate.
The prices of the classroom windows.
水量と確認時刻をそろえた。
服装は関係しない。
名前の調査ではない。
窓の価格ではない。
equal amounts of water and checked them at the same time
発表には何を含めた？
Both experiments.
Only a made-up result.
Nothing about the method.
Only a list of sunny days.
二つの試みを紹介した。
架空の結果ではない。
方法の改善を説明した。
天気一覧だけではない。
Their presentation included both attempts.
syntax: 発表には二つの試みを含めた。
bothは二つともという意味で、複数名詞attemptsを修飾する。

title: 二つの運動場の記憶
paragraphs: For a history project, Kota interviewed two older neighbors about the town's first sports ground. Both remembered playing there as children, but they gave different dates for its opening. One said that it opened when she was seven. The other remembered an opening ceremony several years later. Kota worried that one person must be wrong and that he should remove one interview from his report.
歴史課題でコウタは高齢の近隣住民二人に町初の運動場を取材した。二人とも子供時代に遊んだが、開設年が違った。一人は七歳の時、もう一人は数年後の開場式を覚えていた。どちらかが間違いで、一方の取材を報告から外すべきかと心配した。

He visited the town archive with his teacher. An old newspaper showed a photograph of children playing on an unfinished field. A later article described a ceremony after new seats and changing rooms had been added. [1] The neighbors had remembered different stages of the same place, rather than completely different events.
先生と資料館に行くと、古新聞には未完成の広場で遊ぶ子供の写真があった。後の記事は座席と更衣室の追加後の式を伝えていた。運動場は公式の開場式より前から使われていたのだ。二人は別々の出来事でなく同じ場所の違う段階を覚えていた。

Kota kept both interviews. He used the newspaper dates to explain the difference and asked the neighbors to check his summary. His final report showed how memories and written records could help each other. He learned to ask more questions before deciding that two different answers could not both contain useful information.
コウタは両方の取材を残した。新聞の日付で違いを説明し、二人に要約を確認してもらった。最終報告では記憶と文書が補い合う様子を示した。異なる答えに有用な情報が両方あるはずがないと決める前に、さらに尋ねることを学んだ。
questions: 空所[1]に合う文は？
People had used the ground before its official opening ceremony.
Nobody had ever played on the ground.
The newspapers contained no dates or pictures.
Both neighbors had lived in another country.
使用開始と式の時期が違った。
遊ぶ写真がある。
日付と写真を確認した。
国外居住は理由でない。
children playing on an unfinished field
コウタは何を心配した？
One interview might need to be removed.
The field was still too small for birds.
His neighbors disliked all sports.
The archive had no entrance.
片方を外すべきか迷った。
鳥の話ではない。
二人とも遊んだ記憶がある。
入口は問題でない。
he should remove one interview from his report
最終報告で使った取材は？
Both interviews.
Neither interview.
Only a new television interview.
Only an interview with a player abroad.
二つとも残した。
両方削除していない。
テレビ取材ではない。
海外選手を取材していない。
Kota kept both interviews.
syntax: コウタは二つの取材を残した。
keptはkeepの過去形。bothが二つとも採用したことを示す。

title: 初めて遊ぶ人のために
paragraphs: A group of students made a board game for the school festival. Players moved wooden animals along a river drawn on the board. The students tested it many times and thought the rules were easy. However, when younger children tried the game, several could not begin. They did not know how many cards to take or which animal should move first. The makers had forgotten that they already knew these things.
生徒の班は文化祭用にボードゲームを作った。盤に描いた川に沿い木の動物を動かす。何度も試して規則は簡単だと思ったが、年下の子が試すと始められない子がいた。何枚カードを取るか、どの動物から動かすか不明だった。作り手は自分たちには既知だと忘れていた。

The group watched without explaining anything at first. They wrote down every place where the children stopped. [1] The new page showed the starting position and one complete turn with pictures. The children could point to the pictures while they played. A short example was more useful than another long paragraph of instructions.
班は初め説明せず観察し、子供が止まった箇所を全て記した。そこで遊び始めの例を別紙に作った。新しい紙は初期配置と一回分の手順を絵で示し、子供は遊びながら絵を指せた。長い説明を足すより短い実例が役立った。

At the festival, the game table stayed busy. The makers still answered questions, but they no longer had to explain the beginning to every family. They learned that clear rules should be tested with people who have not helped create them.
文化祭ではゲーム台に人が絶えなかった。質問には答えたが、全家族に最初から説明する必要はなくなった。分かりやすい規則は、制作に関わっていない人に試してもらうべきだと学んだ。
questions: 空所[1]に合う文は？
They then made a separate page with an example of starting the game.
They decided to remove all the pictures.
They told every child to invent new rules.
They closed the festival before anyone arrived.
次の新しい紙の内容につながる。
絵を使って改善した。
規則を子供任せにしない。
文化祭は開かれた。
The new page showed the starting position and one complete turn
子供が最初に困ったことは？
How to start playing.
Where to buy a river.
How to repair the school roof.
Which festival to close.
開始手順が不明だった。
川は盤の絵。
屋根修理ではない。
閉会の相談ではない。
They did not know how many cards to take
規則を誰に試してもらうとよい？
People who did not help make the game.
Only the people who wrote the rules.
Nobody outside the group.
Only people who refuse to play.
制作外の人に試すとよい。
作成者だけでは盲点が残る。
外の人を排除しない。
遊ばない人限定ではない。
people who have not helped create them
syntax: The children could point to the pictures while they played.
子供は遊びながら絵を指すことができた。
couldの後ろは動詞原形。while以下の節は二つの動作の同時進行を示す。

title: 山への荷物を減らす
paragraphs: Before a day trip to a low mountain, Aki filled her bag with many useful things. She packed two large books, extra shoes, three bottles of juice, and a heavy camera. Her friend Ren brought a much smaller bag. Aki thought that he was not ready for changes in the weather. At the meeting place, their guide asked everyone to place their things on a table.
低い山への日帰り旅行の前、アキは役立つ物をたくさん詰めた。大きな本二冊、予備の靴、ジュース三本、重いカメラを入れた。レンはずっと小さな袋で、アキは天気の変化に備えていないと思った。集合場所で案内役は荷物を机に出すよう求めた。

Ren had water, a light rain jacket, lunch, and a small map. Aki's bag contained many things she would probably not use. [1] Together, they checked the route, the weather forecast, and the length of the walk. Aki removed the books and the extra shoes but kept the rain jacket that had been hidden at the bottom.
レンには水、軽い雨具、昼食、小地図があった。アキには使わなそうな物が多かった。案内役は、たくさん運ぶことと必要な物を運ぶことは同じでないと説明した。経路、予報、歩く長さを一緒に確認し、アキは本と予備靴を出したが、底に埋もれた雨具は残した。

On the hill, she was glad that her bag felt lighter. When a short shower came, both friends put on their jackets. Aki learned that preparation meant making choices based on the actual plan, not bringing every object that might be useful somewhere.
山では袋が軽くなりうれしかった。にわか雨の時は二人とも上着を着た。準備とは、どこかで役立ちそうな物を全て持つのでなく、実際の計画に基づき選ぶことだと学んだ。
questions: 空所[1]に入る文は？
The guide explained that more things did not always mean better preparation.
The guide said that nobody needed water.
Ren decided to carry every book in the town.
Aki was told to leave all rain jackets behind.
不要な荷物を減らす判断につながる。
レンは水を持っている。
本を増やす話ではない。
雨具は残して役立った。
Aki removed the books and the extra shoes
二人が一緒に確認したものは？
The route and weather forecast.
The prices of every mountain.
A list of movies for the evening.
The guide's childhood photographs.
経路や予報を確認した。
山の価格ではない。
映画予定ではない。
子供時代の写真でない。
the route, the weather forecast, and the length of the walk
雨が降った時に使ったものは？
Their jackets.
Two large books.
Extra shoes as umbrellas.
A classroom table.
二人とも上着を着た。
本は取り出して置いた。
靴を傘にしていない。
机を運んでいない。
both friends put on their jackets
syntax: Aki removed the books and the extra shoes but kept the rain jacket that had been hidden at the bottom.
the books and the extra shoes
the rain jacket that had been hidden at the bottom
アキは本と予備靴を取り出したが、底に隠れていた雨具は残した。
butが対比する二つの動作をつなぐ。that以下はrain jacketを説明する。

title: 難しい二小節
paragraphs: Saki practiced a short piano piece for a class concert. She liked the opening and played it again and again. However, two bars in the middle were difficult. Each time she reached them, she stopped, felt unhappy, and returned to the beginning. After a week, she could play the opening beautifully, but the middle had hardly improved. She began to think that she was simply not good at music.
サキはクラス演奏会用の短いピアノ曲を練習した。好きな冒頭を何度も弾いたが、中ほどの二小節が難しかった。そこに来ると止まり、落ち込んで初めに戻った。一週間後、冒頭は美しくなっても中ほどはほぼ上達せず、音楽が苦手なのだと思い始めた。

Her teacher asked her to play only the difficult bars very slowly. [1] Saki noticed that one finger had to move before the next note began. Once she understood the movement, she repeated it several times and then joined the bars to the rest of the piece. The whole song became smoother.
先生は難しい小節だけをとてもゆっくり弾くよう頼んだ。初めから毎回弾く代わりに、一つの小さな問題を調べられた。サキは次の音の前に一本の指を動かす必要に気づいた。動きを理解して繰り返し、曲の他の部分とつなぐと全体が滑らかになった。

She still practiced the opening, but she no longer spent all her time there. Her next week's plan gave extra time to the places that needed attention. Saki discovered that a useful practice session was not always the same as an enjoyable performance of the easiest part.
冒頭も練習したが、全時間をそこに費やさなくなった。翌週は注意が必要な箇所に時間を多めに配した。役立つ練習は、一番易しい部分を楽しく弾くことと同じではないと知った。
questions: 空所[1]に合う文は？
This let her examine one small problem instead of always starting again.
This made her forget that the song had a middle.
She was asked to play the opening faster and faster.
The teacher removed all the difficult notes forever.
難しい小部分を調べる流れ。
中ほどに集中している。
速くする指示ではない。
音を削除したのではない。
Saki noticed that one finger had to move
最初の一週間で主に上達した部分は？
The opening.
Only the final silence.
The difficult middle bars.
A different song.
冒頭は美しく弾けた。
無音の話ではない。
中ほどはほぼ改善しなかった。
別の曲ではない。
she could play the opening beautifully
翌週の練習計画は？
Spend extra time on difficult places.
Never touch the piano.
Play only the easiest part.
Stop listening to advice.
注意が要る場所に時間を配した。
練習は続ける。
易しい所だけにはしない。
助言を生かしている。
gave extra time to the places that needed attention
syntax: Her next week's plan gave extra time to the places that needed attention.
to the places that needed attention
翌週の計画では注意の必要な箇所に時間を多めに配した。
that needed attentionはplacesを説明する関係詞節。to以下が時間を配する先を示す。

title: 曇り空の星を見る会
paragraphs: The science club planned an evening for families to look at stars. Members borrowed two telescopes and made a list of bright objects to find. On the afternoon of the event, thick clouds covered the sky. Some members wanted to send everyone a cancellation message. Their leader asked whether the evening had to depend entirely on seeing real stars through a telescope.
科学部は家族向けの星を見る夜を計画した。望遠鏡二台を借り、探す明るい天体を一覧にした。当日の午後は厚い雲に覆われ、中止を知らせたい部員もいた。部長は、本物の星を望遠鏡で見ることだけに夜の活動を頼る必要があるか尋ねた。

They moved tables into the school hall and spread out large sky maps. [1] At one table, children practiced finding north on a map. At another, they learned how to hold and adjust the telescope without moving it toward the sky. Parents asked questions that the club had not expected.
机を講堂に入れて大きな星図を広げた。部員は、晴れた夜に家族が自分で星を探せる準備を手伝うことにした。一つの台では地図上で北を探し、別の台では空に向けず望遠鏡の支え方と調整を習った。保護者からは意外な質問も出た。

The clouds did not clear that night, but most visitors stayed until the end. Each family took home a simple map and the date of the next meeting. The club learned that an event could still be worthwhile when its main plan changed, as long as visitors had something useful to do.
雲は晴れなかったが、大半の来場者は最後までいた。家族は簡単な地図と次回の日程を持ち帰った。主要な計画が変わっても、役立つ活動があれば会は有意義になりうると部は学んだ。
questions: 空所[1]に合う文は？
They decided to help families prepare for a clear night in the future.
They put all maps away and locked the hall.
They promised to remove the clouds by hand.
They asked visitors never to look at stars again.
星図と練習が将来の準備になる。
講堂で活動を行った。
雲を手で動かせない。
次回の予定を知らせた。
children practiced finding north on a map
当日の空はどうだった？
Cloudy.
Clear all evening.
Full of visible stars.
Always sunny indoors.
厚い雲があった。
夜も晴れなかった。
星を見られなかった。
屋内の日照の話でない。
thick clouds covered the sky
家族が持ち帰ったものは？
A map and the next meeting date.
Both telescopes.
All the school tables.
A promise that clouds would disappear.
地図と次回日程。
望遠鏡は借り物。
机は持ち帰っていない。
天候を保証していない。
a simple map and the date of the next meeting
syntax: Parents asked questions that the club had not expected.
questions that the club had not expected
保護者は部が予想していなかった質問をした。
that以下がquestionsを説明する。had not expectedは質問より前の予想を述べる。

title: 島の配達予定
paragraphs: A small island received parcels by boat three times a week. When visitors ordered things online, they sometimes expected delivery the next day. A shopkeeper named Nori often heard complaints when packages arrived later. The online message said that an order had left a warehouse, but it did not show when the island boat would leave the mainland. Strong winds could delay the boat even after a parcel reached the port.
小島には週三回、船で荷物が来た。旅行者が通販すると翌日配達を期待する場合があり、遅れると店主ノリはよく苦情を聞いた。通販の表示は倉庫出発まで分かっても、島の船が本土を出る時刻を示さなかった。港に着いた荷物でも強風で船が遅れることがあった。

Nori made a small board beside his shop. [1] He wrote the next planned boat day and added a note when the port announced a change. He did not promise an exact arrival time for each parcel. Instead, the board helped people understand which part of the journey they were waiting for.
ノリは店の横に小さな板を作り、本土の港から届く知らせを使った。次の出航予定日を書き、港が変更を発表したら追記した。個々の荷物の正確な到着時刻は保証せず、行程のどの段階を待っているか分かるようにした。

Visitors began asking more useful questions. Rather than saying that the shop had lost their parcel, they asked whether the next boat was running. Nori could not change the wind, but clear local information made the wait less confusing for everyone.
来訪者は適切に質問するようになった。店が荷物をなくしたと言う代わりに、次の船が運航するか尋ねた。風は変えられなくても、明確な地域情報で待つ混乱は減った。
questions: 空所[1]に合う文は？
He used updates from the mainland port.
He guessed a new weather report every hour.
He promised to control the wind.
He stopped every boat himself.
港の発表を板に反映した。
予報を創作していない。
風は変えられない。
船を止めていない。
when the port announced a change
船が遅れる原因として出たものは？
Strong winds.
A broken classroom desk.
Too many sky maps.
A closed swimming pool.
強風が原因になりうる。
机は無関係。
星図は出てこない。
プールではない。
Strong winds could delay the boat
板で分かるようにしたことは？
Which stage of delivery people were waiting for.
The exact contents of every private parcel.
A guaranteed arrival minute for every order.
Who should move away from the island.
待つ行程を理解できる。
荷物の中身は掲示しない。
正確な到着は保証しない。
移住を勧めていない。
which part of the journey they were waiting for
syntax: Nori could not change the wind, but clear local information made the wait less confusing for everyone.
clear local information made the wait less confusing for everyone
ノリは風を変えられなかったが、明確な地域情報が皆の待つ混乱を減らした。
butが二つの節を対比する。後半はmake O Cの形で、the waitがless confusingな状態になることを表す。

title: 絵のついた昼食メニュー
paragraphs: At the beginning of the school year, students from several countries joined a lunch club. Each Friday, the members ordered meals from a small restaurant. Some students did not eat meat, and others preferred food without hot peppers. The restaurant had many choices, but its menu used words that new members did not know. Asking a friend to explain every dish took a long time. The club leader, Lisa, wanted everyone to choose a meal without feeling embarrassed. [1] She asked the restaurant owner to check each drawing before printing the new menu. A leaf showed meals without meat, and a pepper showed hot dishes. The pictures did not replace the names or descriptions. They helped students decide which descriptions to read carefully. At the next meeting, ordering took less time, and two new members asked questions about dishes they had never tried. Lisa realized that a small change in information could make joining a group easier.

title: 話す前の一分間
paragraphs: During a class discussion about school uniforms, Mr. Lee noticed that the same four students answered most questions. Other students listened, but he could not tell whether they agreed or had different ideas. He first tried asking everyone to speak in turn. Several students simply repeated the previous answer because they had not prepared their own words. Mr. Lee changed the next discussion. Before anyone spoke, he gave the class one quiet minute to write down an opinion and a reason. [1] Then students compared notes with a partner before talking to the whole class. More hands went up than before. One quiet student pointed out that buying sports clothes and regular uniforms could cost families a lot. Her idea led to a useful discussion of prices. Mr. Lee kept the writing time in later lessons. He did not expect every student to become a confident speaker immediately, but he wanted everyone to have a fair chance to think.

制服についての話し合いで、リー先生はいつも同じ四人が答えることに気づいた。他の生徒が賛成なのか別の考えなのか分からなかった。順番に全員を当てると、準備できず前の人の答えを繰り返す生徒もいた。次は発言前に一分間、静かに意見と理由を書かせた。これで生徒は自分の答えを考える時間を得た。その後、隣の人とメモを比べてから全体で話した。挙手が増え、普段静かな生徒が、運動着と制服の両方は家計に負担だと指摘して価格の議論になった。先生は以後も書く時間を設けた。すぐに全員が自信ある話し手になるとは期待せず、公平に考える機会を与えたかった。
